defects: Finite sublevel-set condition is given as an explicit hypothesis (∀ B : ℝ, Set.Finite {x | h x ≤ B}) rather than via the gold's [Northcott h] typeclass instance; mathematically equivalent (assuming Northcott h is defined as exactly this property) but a structural mismatch rather than a pure notational one.

The existential hypothesis '∃ n b c, 1 < b ∧ ∀ x, h(x^n) ≥ b*h x - c' replaces the gold's use of n, b, c₀ as free/implicit theorem parameters with separate hypotheses hb and H; logically equivalent (since the conclusion doesn't depend on n, b, c) but a different quantifier structure, not mere renaming/reordering.

Conclusion is stated as Set.Finite (CommGroup.torsion G : Set G) (finiteness of the coerced Set) instead of gold's Finite (torsion G) (finiteness of the subtype); equivalent via Set.finite_coe_iff but syntactically a different formulation.
